name: Corporation Park Community Orchard
short_description: Heritage apple trees in Corporation Park.
description: A collection of apple and pear trees in the walled garden area of Corporation Park. Fruit is free to pick for visitors throughout the autumn season.

name: Witton Country Park Blackberries
short_description: Brambles along the woodland edges at Witton Country Park.
description: Extensive blackberry brambles line the footpaths and woodland margins throughout Witton Country Park. Plentiful picking from late August into October.

name: Incredible Edible Blackburn (Town Centre)
short_description: Edible planters in Blackburn town centre.
description: Community-maintained raised planters near the market and Cathedral Quarter growing herbs, kale and edible flowers for free picking.

name: Witton Country Park Sloes
short_description: Blackthorn hedgerows throughout Witton Country Park.
description: Dense blackthorn bushes in the park's open areas produce heavy crops of sloes each autumn. Best picked after the first frost in October.

name: Ewood Allotments Surplus Stall
short_description: Honesty-box surplus veg from Ewood allotments.
description: Plot holders put out surplus vegetables including beans, courgettes and tomatoes on a free-sharing table at the allotment entrance during the growing season.

name: Billinge Wood Wild Garlic
short_description: Wild garlic in the ancient woodland of Billinge Wood.
description: Carpets of wild garlic cover the floor of Billinge Wood each spring. The woodland is best visited in April when the white flowers are in bloom.

name: Pleasington Playing Fields Elderberries
short_description: Elder trees along the hedgerows at Pleasington.
description: Elder trees grow along the hedgerows and field margins surrounding Pleasington Playing Fields. Elderflower in June and berries from late August.

name: Blackburn Community Growing Hub (Bastwell)
short_description: Community veg beds with free surplus produce in Bastwell.
description: A neighbourhood growing project with raised beds producing seasonal vegetables. Surplus is placed on a sharing table at the site entrance throughout summer.

name: Darwen Moor Bilberries
short_description: Bilberries on the open moorland above Darwen.
description: Wild bilberries ripen across the heather moorland of Darwen Moor in mid to late summer. Best picked in July and August on the paths around Darwen Tower.

name: Audley Range Incredible Edible Planters
short_description: Edible herb planters on Audley Range.
description: Volunteer-maintained street planters growing rosemary, mint, chives and parsley. Residents and passers-by are encouraged to take what they need.

name: Sunnyhurst Wood Hazelnuts
short_description: Hazel coppice in Sunnyhurst Wood near Darwen.
description: Hazel trees are abundant throughout Sunnyhurst Wood, a popular ancient woodland south of Blackburn. Nuts are ready to pick from September.

name: Fishmoor Reservoir Path Blackberries
short_description: Brambles along the Fishmoor Reservoir footpath.
description: The public footpath skirting Fishmoor Reservoir is lined with productive blackberry brambles throughout late summer and early autumn.

name: Witton Country Park Hazelnuts
short_description: Hazel trees in the ancient woodland section of Witton Park.
description: Hazel coppice can be found in the older wooded areas of Witton Country Park. Nuts are typically ready to harvest from mid-September.

name: Blackburn Cathedral Garden Herbs
short_description: Edible herb garden at Blackburn Cathedral.
description: A small but productive herb garden maintained by volunteers in the Cathedral precinct. Visitors are welcome to pick herbs including sage, thyme and lavender.

name: Roddlesworth Woods Wild Garlic
short_description: Wild garlic in Roddlesworth Woods near Darwen.
description: The ancient woodland walks of Roddlesworth are carpeted in wild garlic each spring. A beautiful and productive foraging walk along the reservoir paths.

name: The Greenhouse Project Community Garden
short_description: Community garden with orchard
description: soft fruit area and vegetable beds. Volunteers often share produce with the local community.
